name: 2x2
notes: The 3x3's smaller, corners-only cousin — no edge pieces means fewer parity headaches.

name: 3x3
notes: The one that started it. Still the puzzle I reach for when I want to think about something else.

name: 4x4
notes: Adds a parity problem the 3x3 doesn't have: even layers mean some scrambles need extra algorithms to fix.

name: 5x5
notes: Big enough to have real center and edge pieces to build, not just twist into place.

name: 6x6
notes: Even-layered like the 4x4, but large enough that reduction takes a while before it even looks like a cube.

name: 1x3x3
notes: Folds flat instead of twisting — more fidget toy than puzzle some days.

name: Pyraminx
notes: Four axial turns solve most of it in seconds — the real puzzle is the trickier tips on the last layer.

name: Megaminx
notes: A dodecahedral 3x3 — twelve faces instead of six, and a last layer that takes twice as long.

name: Square-1
notes: Reshapes into all kinds of parallelograms mid-solve — barely looks like a cube half the time.

name: Skewb
notes: Turns through its corners instead of faces, so every twist reshuffles the whole puzzle at once.

name: Polaris Cube
notes: A Skewb that also turns vertically and horizontally once twisted partway open.

name: Six Spot Cube
notes: A 3x3 shape mod with six center pieces swapped, so it never looks fully solved even when it is.

name: Mirror Cube
notes: Same cuts as a 3x3, but every piece is a different size — solved by shape, not color.

name: Ghost Cube
notes: Sheared into odd angles — looks scrambled even when it's solved.

name: Master Morphix
notes: A 3x3 mechanism hiding inside a shape-shifting tetrahedron.

name: Duomo Cube
notes: A mashup of Pyraminx and Master Morphix — the color scramble looks worse than it is.

name: Puppet Cube
notes: A 3x3 hidden inside a 2x2 shell. Deceptively hard to read.

name: Axis Cube
notes: Cut at an angle so solved and scrambled states can look confusingly similar from across the room.

name: Fisher Cube
notes: A 3x3 twisted 45 degrees on its core — same mechanism, disorienting new shape.

name: Windmill Cube
notes: Some layers shift diagonally instead of turning flat, so it drifts into a pinwheel shape mid-solve.

name: Pentacle Cube
notes: A five-pointed star shape mod hiding a 3x3 mechanism underneath the points.

name: Gear Cube
notes: Interlocking gears mean one turn moves more than one layer at once.

name: Curvy Copter
notes: Edge-turning with curved cuts that let it fold into non-cube shapes mid-solve.

name: Infinity Cube
notes: Less a twisty puzzle, more an endless-folding fidget toy — still earns a shelf spot.
